data: The most important things to know in your first week shipping Quiz Lab.
Where do quiz pack JSON files live in the repo?
Packs are single JSON files in app/src/lib/data/packs/, one file per pack; the packs index picks them up automatically (Pack Authoring Guide; Architecture Overview).
Where is the live Quiz Lab app hosted?
The app is a static site served from GitHub Pages under the base path /product-demo. There is no Vercel deployment — that claim only appears in aspirational marketing copy (Architecture Overview).
What actually triggers a production deploy of Quiz Lab?
Running a manual `npm run deploy` command
Merging a PR to `main`, which a GitHub Actions workflow builds and publishes
Clicking 'Promote to Production' in a hosting dashboard

The entire pipeline is: merge to main → GitHub Actions builds the static site → it publishes to GitHub Pages. There is no separate deploy step or manual release (Engineering Handbook; Architecture Overview).
What database does Quiz Lab use to store packs and leaderboards?
None — it is a fully prerendered static app with no backend
Quiz Lab has no server runtime and no database; all content ships in the build as static files. Any mention of Postgres or a backend is outdated or marketing material (Architecture Overview).
Which framework and build setup does Quiz Lab use?
Plain React with a custom Express server
Quiz Lab is a SvelteKit app built with Vite and the static adapter; everything is prerendered at build time, so there is no server runtime (Architecture Overview).
How does new code reach the `main` branch?
Through a reviewed pull request that is squash-merged
Pushed to a release branch and cherry-picked
Emailed to a maintainer who applies the patch
The team practices trunk-based development: you never commit directly to main — all work lands through a reviewed, squash-merged pull request (Engineering Handbook).
How many reviewer approvals does a PR need before it can merge?
Every PR needs one reviewer approval before merge (Engineering Handbook, Review standards).
What must pass in `app/` before a pack PR can merge, since a failure blocks the Pages deploy?
`npm run build` (in app/) must succeed with the new pack registered; a broken build blocks the GitHub Pages deploy (Architecture Overview; Pack Authoring Guide).
Which development model best describes how the team works?
Gitflow with long-lived develop and release branches
The team practices trunk-based development: main is always releasable and branches are short-lived, opened as small PRs and reviewed within a day (Engineering Handbook).
How many choices must each quiz question have?
The Pack Authoring Guide requires exactly 4 options in each question's `choices` array.
How is the correct answer for a question stored in a pack?
As a `correct` string holding the answer text
As a `correctIndex` integer from 0 to 3 indexing into `choices`
By marking the choice object with `isCorrect: true`
As the first item in the `answers` array
Each question stores `correctIndex`, an integer 0–3 that indexes into the four `choices`. Storing the answer as a string is the deprecated v0 format and is no longer valid (Pack Authoring Guide).
How many questions should a pack contain?
The Pack Authoring Guide specifies 10–15 questions per pack, with mixed difficulty (1–3).
Which sequence describes how work flows through Studio AI from start to ship?
idea → tasks → pick up task → branch → PR → review → merge → done
Work flows idea → tasks → pick up task → branch → PR → review → merge (ships) → task done. Merging auto-transitions the task to done and ships to GitHub Pages (Studio AI SDLC & MCP Workflow).
What is the single highest-leverage thing you can do for a coding agent's output quality?
Give it the largest possible context dump of every document
Curate a small neighborhood (~5 docs) of the most relevant context at task pickup
Let it search the whole knowledge base on its own each time
Run it with no context so it stays unbiased

Giving an agent a small, curated neighborhood (~5 docs) of the most relevant context up front is the cheapest, highest-leverage lever on quality; agents left to search wander, burn tokens, and drift off scope (Engineering Handbook; Studio AI SDLC & MCP Workflow).
